# Results (generated by `itb analyze`)

tau: +1 = the earlier probe in the block always had the higher price (price) / was written first (arrival); 0 = unrelated. Head-to-head: only pairs where the higher-priced probe was written later; +1 = price always won, -1 = arrival always won. p: permutation test within blocks; q: Benjamini–Hochberg within each level of this table (validators, clients, client + mode); a rule is claimed only at q < 0.05 with at least 10 pairs from at least 4 blocks — fewer blocks are shown but not judged. [lo, hi]: 95% interval of tau from a block-level bootstrap (2000 resamples of whole blocks). Detectable |tau|: the smallest effect the cell would find with 80% power at p < 0.05, from its own permutation null (95th percentile of |tau| plus 0.84 null standard deviations; normal approximation, before the multiple-testing correction) — "no rule detected" means no rule at least that strong, not that the order is random. Landed: all located probes (in the targeted leader's own blocks — the only ones used). Position: 0 = top of block, 1 = bottom.

## Secondary evidence: the rest of the block

Not from our own transactions, so it supports the main result but cannot replace it. For every block of a targeted leader that holds one of our probes, the other transactions are compared pair by pair: fee per CU tau +1 would mean the block is sorted by fee per compute unit, highest first. Fee per CU is the fee above the 5000-lamport base fee divided by consumed CU — an approximation: the price is charged on the requested CU limit, which a block does not record, multi-signature transactions pay several base fees, and Jito bundle tips are paid by transfer, not by fee. "Outpaid, placed below": of the transactions that paid more per CU than one of our probes, the share that sits after it in the block (0 if the block were sorted by fee per CU).
